## 1. Gradient checks (`tests/gradcheck`)

Central differences with h = 10⁻⁶ in float64, on L = Σ f(x) ⊙ R for a random fixed tensor R (so off-diagonal Jacobian errors cannot cancel). Relative deviation |a − n| / max(|a|, |n|, 10⁻⁷). Tolerance: 10⁻⁵. A deliberately wrong rule is shown to fail with relative deviation > 0.3, so the check is not vacuous.

## 2. TF.js parity (`tests/parity`)

For each planned architecture, TF.js 4.22 (CPU backend, float32, its own autodiff) trains the same network from identical seeded initial weights on the identical batch order, independently of our engine (float64, per-sample accumulation). Criterion at every step: |ours − tf| ≤ 10⁻⁴ + 10⁻³·|tf| for the batch loss and for every parameter. Rationale in ADR-009.

| Architecture | Steps | Parameters | Max |Δ loss| | Max |Δ param| | Final loss (ours / TF.js) | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CNN (conv3x3 p1 ReLU, maxpool2, conv3x3 s1, avgpool2, flatten, dense softmax) | 102 | 157 | 1.14e-7 | 3.88e-7 | 0.7035474 / 0.7035473 | yes |
| CNN experiment 8 (conv3x3×4 ReLU, maxpool2, flatten, dense softmax) on reduced MNIST 28×28 | 108 | 2071 | 1.04e-6 | 1.25e-6 | 1.288356e-11 / 0 (exact) | yes |
| CNN with strided, padded convolution (conv3x3 s2 p1 sigmoid, maxpool2, flatten, dense sigmoid) | 102 | 47 | 1.44e-7 | 3.21e-7 | 1.066803 / 1.066803 | yes |
| Vanishing gradients (2-4-4-4-4-1 sigmoid stack) | 100 | 77 | 5.40e-8 | 4.30e-7 | 0.7189838 / 0.7189838 | yes |
| Gradient descent (linear neuron, MSE) | 100 | 2 | 1.58e-7 | 3.90e-7 | 0.008838404 / 0.008838399 | yes |
| Forward/backprop MLP (2-8-3, ReLU, softmax + CCE, momentum) | 102 | 51 | 2.22e-7 | 7.29e-7 | 0.5438356 / 0.5438356 | yes |
| XOR with an MLP (2-4-1, tanh/sigmoid, BCE) | 100 | 17 | 1.07e-7 | 7.27e-7 | 0.1592764 / 0.1592764 | yes |
| Single neuron / logistic unit | 100 | 3 | 2.88e-7 | 5.78e-7 | 0.03778722 / 0.03778720 | yes |

*Table note.* Final loss is the mean loss of the last mini-batch, printed at full precision (7 significant digits; scientific notation below 10⁻³). A value shown as "0 (exact)" is an exact floating-point zero, not a rounded display.

**Why the reduced-MNIST case ends near zero (`reports/mnist-fit.json`, `npx tsx scripts/measure-mnist-fit.ts`).** The parity case trains on only 60 images (20 per class of the digits 0, 1, 2) for 9 epochs (108 steps), deliberately small so the float32 reference stays fast. The network fits these images perfectly:
- training accuracy 100 %;
- smallest log-probability margin between the correct class and the strongest competitor 8.7 nats, median 26.6;
- per-example loss at most 1.67e-4, mean 7.15e-6.

The last mini-batch (5 images) has a mean loss of 1.288356e-11 in DL-VizLab's float64 arithmetic: small, not zero. TF.js computes in float32. When 1 − p for the correct class falls below 2⁻²⁴ ≈ 6 × 10⁻⁸ (true for 50 of the 60 images), float32 rounds p to exactly 1, so the loss −log p is exactly 0. The 0 in the TF.js column is therefore genuine float32 behaviour, not a formatting artefact. For the same reason, the relative loss deviation of this case is not meaningful (the denominator is 0); parity is judged by the absolute criterion above, which every step meets. The full experiment (1 500 training and 300 held-out images) does not reach this regime: its final training loss is 0.025 and its held-out accuracy 97.0 % (PROGRESS, P7).

The overlay plot `figures/parity-overlay.pdf` shows the two loss curves for the XOR experiment and the CNN on top of each other, with the per-step absolute differences below.
